_meta.value: Toyota Fortuner 2.8 diesel AT 4x4 (India, 2021 facelift onward; Legender noted where it differs)
_meta.notes: Compiled 2026-11-18. Classes: official = Toyota (India where available; other Toyota distributors labelled by market), independent = road tests and catalogues, estimate = derived (formula in notes), assumption = typical body-on-frame SUV value, NOT Fortuner data. Where sources conflict, both are kept as separate keys with a suffix. Toyota India lists rpm in s^-1; multiply by 60 for rpm. Legender 4x4 AT has the same mechanical specs as Fortuner 4x4 AT in the Toyota India spec sheets (same engine rating, tyres, suspension, GVW); it differs in styling and equipment only.

engine_code.notes: Toyota UK Hilux tech spec; Toyota Pakistan (Indus) Fortuner spec sheet also says '1GD-FTV Hi with Balance Shaft' (https://toyota-indus.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Spec-Sheet-Toyota-Fortuner-GR-S.pdf). Toyota India brochure does not print the engine code.

displacement_cc.notes: Toyota global 2015 GD launch release says 2,754 cc (https://global.toyota/detail/8348091). Rounding difference only.

cylinders.notes: 4-cylinder in-line, DOHC 16-valve. Toyota Pakistan sheet adds 'with Balance Shaft'.

bore_mm.notes: Same 92 x 103.6 in Toyota global release https://global.toyota/detail/8348091 and drom.ru Fortuner 2.8 AT entry.

firing_order.notes: NOT verified for the 1GD-FTV. 1-3-4-2 is the standard inline-4 order; no 1GD-specific source found. For audio: an inline-4 four-stroke fires twice per crank revolution, so firing frequency (Hz) = rpm / 30.

turbo_type.notes: Toyota global release: 'compact high-efficiency variable geometry turbocharger (produced in-house by Toyota)' https://global.toyota/detail/8348091

peak_power_kw_AT.notes: AT: @ 50-57 s^-1 = 3000-3420 rpm. Toyota UK and Toyota Pakistan: 3,000-3,400 rpm.

peak_torque_rpm_range_AT.notes: Printed as 27-47 s^-1 (1620-2820 rpm); rounded to 1600-2800 per Toyota UK sheet.

pre_facelift_rating_for_reference.notes: Use only to interpret older Indian road tests (2016-2020), which were run on this rating.

gr_s_rating_note.value: India GR-S: 204 PS / 500 Nm (same as standard AT)
gr_s_rating_note.notes: Wikipedia lists a 165 kW / 550 Nm GR Sport tune for other markets (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_GD_engine); Autocar India gives 204 hp for the India GR-S.

idle_rpm.source: none: no Fortuner/1GD idle-speed figure found
idle_rpm.notes: NOT Fortuner data. Typical warm idle for a modern passenger common-rail diesel is about 700-800 rpm. Replace with a measured value (an OBD reading from a real car) when available.

max_engine_speed_rpm.notes: Wikipedia infobox 'max engine speed'; no Toyota source found for redline or fuel cut. Related data point: a Peugeot 1.5 BlueHDi recording notes that pump caps at 4000 rpm (different engine). Treat fuel cut as 4400-4600 until verified.

torque_curve_AT_estimate.notes: NO dyno chart or published Toyota curve was found; this curve is built from peak values. 1600-2800: official 500 Nm plateau. 3000/3200/3400: T = P/omega with official 150 kW (150000/(2*pi*rpm/60)) = 477.5/447.6/421.3 Nm. 1200: 500*(370/450) = 411 Nm, scaling the 2015 release's '370 Nm @ 1200 rpm' for the 450 Nm engine (https://global.toyota/detail/8348091). 1400: linear interpolation. 750 and 1000 rpm: assumption (turbo not spooled). 3600/4000/4400: assumption of power falling to about 145/130/110 kW past the power band. Replace with a measured dyno sheet if one is found.

torque_curve_MT_estimate.notes: Plateau 420 Nm 1400-3400 is official. 420 Nm at 3400 rpm = 149.5 kW, consistent with 150 kW. Points below 1400 and above 3400 are assumptions.

engine_rotating_inertia.variant: generic 2.5-3.0 L 4-cyl diesel incl. flywheel/flexplate and torque-converter impeller
engine_rotating_inertia.notes: NOT Fortuner data. A typical tuning range for sims is 0.15-0.35 kg*m^2. Tune by matching free-rev rate in recordings.

transmission.value: Aisin AC60F 6-speed torque-converter automatic, sequential shift + paddles
transmission.notes: Toyota Pakistan spec sheet lists the code AC60F for Fortuner GR-S/Legender/Sigma 4 (1GD). Toyota India: '6AT [Sequential Shift + Paddle Shift + Shiftlock]'. CarExpert AU also gives AC60F.

gear_ratios_AT.variant: Hilux 2.8 6AT (Toyota UK); same set listed for Fortuner 2.8 AT (Russia) by drom.ru
gear_ratios_AT.notes: Official figures are for the Hilux, which shares the 1GD/AC60F. Fortuner-specific confirmation: https://www.drom.ru/catalog/toyota/fortuner/305818/ (independent catalogue, same ratios). gearboxlist.com gives the same AC60F set.

final_drive_AT.notes: Toyota UK gives 3.909 for the Hilux 2.8 6AT (official, sister vehicle): https://media.toyota.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/pdf/220217M-Hilux-Tech-Spec.pdf. No Toyota India figure found. A South African forum notes Toyota does not publish the Fortuner final drive.

gear_ratios_MT_reference.notes: For reference only (the sim target is the AT). Not verified for the Indian Fortuner MT.

transfer_high_ratio.notes: Not printed by Toyota; implied by the crawl-ratio math (see transfer_low_ratio). Toyota part-time transfers are 1:1 in high.

transfer_low_ratio.notes: Derived: 4x4 Australia publishes crawl ratio 36.1:1 (auto) and 44.0:1 (manual). Low = 36.1 / (3.600 x 3.909) = 2.565; manual check 44.0 / (4.784 x 3.583) = 2.567. Both match the 2.566 low ratio Toyota uses in its VF-family transfers (Lexus GX tech doc, seen in a search snippet only). The test car was the 2016 450 Nm version; the gearbox and transfer are assumed unchanged.

torque_converter_stall_rpm.notes: No published stall speed found. Typical stall for a diesel SUV TC is about 1800-2400 rpm (assumption, NOT Fortuner data).

shift_points.notes: No test reports shift rpm. Qualitative: 4x4 Australia says the 6AT 'shifts back a gear at the slightest incline' and drops back quickly to control descent speed. Suggested sim default (assumption): upshift at about 2200-2600 rpm part throttle and about 3600-3800 rpm at full throttle (power band ends at 3400). Drive modes ECO/NORMAL/SPORT are official (Toyota India).

kerb_weight_kg_MY_official.notes: Gross 2,740 kg. Toyota India does NOT publish kerb weight in its spec sheet.

kerb_weight_kg_AU.notes: GVM 3,100 kg (AU rating). A CarExpert 2021 GX search snippet said 2130 kg unladen (low confidence, not fetched).

kerb_weight_kg_IN_aggregators.notes: Search-snippet values only: 91wheels 2180, carbikebhp 4x4 AT 2190, Team-BHP spec page 2220 (probably the MT). CarDekho's 4WD AT page shows 2560 kg, which is likely a data error (close to GVW). Suggested sim value: 2180 kg plus driver.

axle_weight_split_front.unit: fraction of kerb weight on front axle
axle_weight_split_front.variant: generic front-engine body-on-frame diesel 7-seat SUV, unladen
axle_weight_split_front.source: none: no Fortuner axle-load figure found
axle_weight_split_front.notes: NOT Fortuner data. Typical 52-55% front unladen; shifts rearward with passengers and luggage.

length_mm.notes: Printed 479.5 cm. drom.ru Russia lists 4870 (different bumpers).

track_front_mm.notes: Not printed by Toyota India. Same 1545/1555 in the Malaysia brochure and drom.ru.

ground_clearance_mm_IN_autocar.notes: drom.ru (Russia) also 225. CarDekho India 4WD AT page: 220 mm unladen.

ground_clearance_mm_PK_MY_official.notes: Toyota's 'min running ground clearance' figure; measured differently from the 225 mm figure. Conflict kept.

approach_angle_deg.notes: Printed 0.51 rad = 29.2 deg. Australian sources: 29 deg.

departure_angle_deg.notes: Printed 0.44 rad = 25.2 deg. Australian sources: 25 deg.

rampover_angle_deg.notes: Toyota India does not publish this.

turning_radius_m.notes: Printed 580 cm (Toyota tyre-based). Toyota Pakistan lists 'Min. Turning Radius Body 6.2 m'. AU turning circle 11.6 m (snippet only).

suspension_front.value: Independent double wishbone, coil springs, stabiliser bar
suspension_front.notes: Coil spring and stabiliser wording from the Malaysia brochure.

suspension_rear.value: Rigid axle, 4-link with coil springs, lateral control rod (Panhard), stabiliser bar
suspension_rear.variant: Malaysia brochure wording; India says '4-Link With Coil Spring'
suspension_rear.notes: Malaysia: '4-link coil Spring with Lateral Control Rod & Stabiliser'. Toyota India: 4-link with coil spring, stabiliser front and rear, plus 'Pitch & Bounce Control' (4WD/Legender). CONFLICT: Autocar India's spec page says 'independent multi-link', which is likely a data error. Pakistan GR-S adds monotube shock absorbers.

tyre_size_4x4.notes: 2WD Fortuner and petrol: 265/65 R17. Legender (2WD and 4WD): 265/60 R18 per the Legender spec sheet.

tyre_oe_brand.notes: No source names the factory-fitted brand for Indian 2021+ 4x4 cars. Malaysia brochure says 'Highway Terrain' tyres on the 18-inch fitment. Check a real car's sidewall.

tyre_overall_diameter_mm.notes: 18 x 25.4 + 2 x (265 x 0.60) = 457.2 + 318 = 775.2 mm. Nominal rolling radius about 0.375 m (unloaded 0.3876 x ~0.97 loaded-rolling factor, an assumption).

wheel_size.notes: 18-inch alloys on India 4x4 (official tyre size). Rim width not published by Toyota India.

brakes.value: Ventilated discs front and rear; front 4-piston fixed caliper
brakes.notes: Caliper: https://www.toyota.com.my/content/dam/malaysia/model-brochures/brochures/Fortuner-E-brochure-2023-v2.pdf. Note the Hilux uses rear drums, the Fortuner rear discs.

brake_disc_front_mm.unit: mm diameter x 28 mm thick, ventilated
brake_disc_front_mm.variant: Fortuner N15/N16 2.7 petrol 4x4 TGN156 (2015-) parts catalogue
brake_disc_front_mm.notes: Petrol TGN156 fitment; the diesel GUN156 is assumed to share it (an aftermarket kit title says '338mm rotors for Toyota Fortuner GUN156', search snippet only). Not verified for the 1GD.

brake_disc_rear_mm.unit: mm diameter x 18 mm thick, ventilated

brake_aids.value: ABS, EBD, BA, VSC, TRC, A-TRC (4WD), HAC, DAC (4WD), Emergency Brake Signal

steering_type.value: Rack and pinion, hydraulic power assist with VFC (Variable Flow Control), tilt and telescopic
steering_type.notes: Rack & pinion wording from the Malaysia brochure. Autocar India calls it heavy at parking speeds.

steering_ratio_overall.source: none: no Fortuner steering ratio found
steering_ratio_overall.notes: NOT Fortuner data. Derived from assumed lock-to-lock 3.5 turns (630 deg of wheel each way from centre) over an estimated mean road-wheel lock of about 32 deg: 630/32 = 19.7, rounded.

steering_lock_to_lock_turns.notes: NOT Fortuner data; no review found quoting it.

max_outer_wheel_steer_angle_deg.notes: Bicycle-model estimate: asin(wheelbase / R) = asin(2.745 / 5.8) = 28.2 deg for the outer front wheel. Inner wheel would be about 35-37 deg with Ackermann (assumption).

drag_coefficient_Cd.notes: No published Fortuner Cd found. The Hilux shares front structure and a similar frontal shape; the Fortuner's closed wagon body probably differs by a few hundredths. Typical SUV range 0.35-0.45.

frontal_area_m2.notes: A = 0.85 x width x height = 0.85 x 1.855 x 1.835 = 2.89 m^2. The 0.85 fill factor is an assumption for boxy SUVs. CdA = 0.394 x 2.89 = 1.14 m^2.

rolling_resistance_coeff.variant: generic H/T SUV tyre on asphalt
rolling_resistance_coeff.notes: NOT Fortuner data. Use about 0.03-0.08 for gravel and dirt.

drivetrain_4wd_system.value: Part-time 4WD: H2 / H4 / L4 via electronic dial ('Electronic Drive [2WD/4WD] Control'), Automatic Disconnecting Differential (ADD) at front
drivetrain_4wd_system.notes: Pakistan: 'Part-Time H2, H4, L4, Switch Type'. Malaysia: 'Part-time 4WD with Automatic Disconnecting Differential (ADD)'. No centre differential: H4/L4 lock front and rear shafts, so avoid tyre wind-up on high-grip surfaces in the sim.

rear_diff_lock.value: Electric rear differential lock (button); engages only in L4
rear_diff_lock.variant: Fortuner 4x4 (Australia 2021 review); India lists 'Lockable Differential - 4WD Variants'
rear_diff_lock.notes: CarExpert: only engages in low range; most electronic aids are disabled when it is engaged; engagement can be delayed while the indicator flashes. India 'Lockable Differential' is official (Toyota India spec sheet).

auto_lsd.notes: Listed as 'Auto-Limited Slip Differential'. Toyota's Auto LSD is a TRC-based brake function, not a mechanical LSD (general Toyota knowledge, not sourced here).

driver_aids.value: VSC with BA, TRC, A-TRC, HAC, DAC (4WD only), ABS+EBD
driver_aids.notes: A-TRC brakes a spinning wheel to send torque across an open diff (Malaysia brochure: 'the system brakes that wheel and transfers' torque).

dac_behaviour.value: Button-activated below 30 km/h in L4 (some sources say L4 or H4); brakes each wheel to hold a low descent speed; DAC lamp on and slip lamp flashing while active
dac_behaviour.notes: Gridoto, citing the Fortuner owner's manual: activates in L4 or H4 below 30 km/h. It will not activate with the rear diff locked, in P, with the accelerator or brake pressed, above 30 km/h, or with overheated brakes. Toyota India lists DAC for 4WD variants only. Related official Toyota manual (2025 Tacoma OM04011U, different vehicle): https://assets.sia.toyota.com/publications/en/om-x/OM04011U/topics/chapter4/ch04se050431.html. It describes a selectable 4-30 km/h target, cancellation above about 30 km/h, and that the stop lamps light. No Fortuner target descent speed found; sim suggestion (assumption): hold about 5-7 km/h in L4.

hac_behaviour.value: Hill-start assist holds brake pressure briefly after releasing the brake on an incline
hac_behaviour.notes: Fitment is official (HAC listed). The hold duration (about 2 s) is a typical Toyota value, NOT verified for the Fortuner.

perf_braking_autocar_80_0_older.notes: Snippet only, different generation. Listed only to show the spread.

top_speed_kmh_claimed.notes: Toyota India publishes no top speed. Aggregators (91wheels) list 190 km/h, snippet only, low.

derived_kmh_per_1000rpm.unit: km/h per 1000 rpm in gears 1-6 (H range, no TC slip)
derived_kmh_per_1000rpm.notes: v = 1000 / (gear x 3.909) x 2*pi*r x 60/1000, with r = 0.3876 m unloaded (circumference 2.435 m). 6th at 100 km/h is about 1550 rpm. 180 km/h is about 3310 rpm in 5th and 2795 rpm in 6th; 5th reaches the 4600 rpm limit at about 250 km/h, so top speed is limited by drag, not gearing. 1st reaches 3400 rpm at about 35 km/h. Using a loaded rolling radius (about 0.375 m) gives about 3% lower speeds. In L4, divide by 2.566.
